
The estimated [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of $\esurv(t)$ at a single time point $t$ is given
by **Greenwood's formula**:

:::{#thm-greenwood}
#### Greenwood's estimator for variance of Kaplan-Meier survival estimator

$$
\varhf{\esurv(t)} = \esurv(t)^2\sum_{t_i \le t}\frac{d_i}{r_i(r_i-d_i)}
$$ {#eq-var-est-surv}

[@klein2003survival, Section 4.2, eq. (4.2.2)]
:::

We can use @eq-var-est-surv for [confidence intervals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) for a survival
function or a difference of [survival functions](#def-surv-fn).

{{< slidebreak >}}

### Understanding Greenwood's formula (optional)

::: notes
To see where Greenwood's formula comes from, let $x_i = r_i - d_i$. We
approximate the solution treating each time as [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt), with $r_i$
fixed and ignore randomness in times of failure and we treat $x_i$ as
independent [binomials](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-binomial) $\dBinf{r_i, p_i}$. Letting $\surv(t)$ be the
"true" survival function
:::

$$
\ba
\esurv(t) &=\prod_{t_i \le t}x_i/r_i\\
\surv(t)&=\prod_{t_i \le t}p_i
\ea
$$

$$
\ba
\frac{\esurv(t)}{\surv(t)}
&= \prod_{t_i \le t} \frac{x_i}{p_i r_i}
\\ &= \prod_{t_i \le t} \frac{\hat p_i}{p_i}
\\ &= \prod_{t_i \le t} \paren{1+\frac{\hat p_i-p_i}{p_i}}
\\ &\approx 1+\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{\hat p_i-p_i}{p_i}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

$$
\ba
\Varf{\frac{\esurv(t)}{\surv(t)}}
&\approx \Varf{1+\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{\hat p_i-p_i}{p_i}}
\\ &=\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{1}{p_i^2}\frac{p_i(1-p_i)}{r_i}
\\ &= \sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{(1-p_i)}{p_i r_i}
\\ &\approx\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{(1-x_i/r_i)}{x_i}
\\ &=\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{r_i-x_i}{x_i r_i}
\\ &=\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{d_i}{r_i(r_i-d_i)}
\\ \tf \Varf{\esurv(t)}
&\approx \esurv(t)^2\sum_{t_i \le t} \frac{d_i}{r_i(r_i-d_i)}
\ea
$$
